summary: The prior CMC-linked CRL remains the main adverse evidence for UX111. Resubmission acceptance does not establish manufacturing resolution, while sponsor-reported favorable clinical interpretations and longer follow-up provide limited detail for assessing benefit.
pivotalQuestion: Does the resubmission resolve the prior manufacturing findings and provide adequate biomarker and clinical support for accelerated approval?

factors.rationale: Ultragenyx describes clinical and biomarker evidence favorably and reports longer follow-up, but supplied summaries provide no interpretable efficacy results. The trial is nonrandomized and open-label.
No candidate-specific safety findings are supplied in this packet.
The prior CRL requested CMC improvements and manufacturing-inspection information. Resubmission acceptance and the latest sponsor update do not establish that these documented issues are resolved.
Ultragenyx reports acceptance of the accelerated-approval BLA resubmission, reaffirmed in its August update. This is procedural progress, not confirmation of clinical or manufacturing adequacy.
